With a surprising tone all its own, the Big Muff Pi 2 made waves when the original circuit from the 1970s was resurrected in collaboration with Josh Scott of JHS Pedals. This take on the iconic pedal is optimized for bass players looking for a tasty fuzz without sacrificing any low-end flavor. The Bass Big Muff 2 features the signature midrange grind of the original with the flexible EQ and virtually endless sustain expected in any Big Muff. The Bass version adds a BLEND knob and BASS BOOST switch to the VOL, SUSTAIN, TONE control set. The BLEND knob mixes the dry and fuzz signals to set the perfect balance of distortion without losing clarity and foundational low-end. Flip the BASS BOOST switch to make an even bigger impact, especially while running the TONE knob at higher, more trebly settings. These added controls let the bass player dial in the best fuzz tone without sacrificing their ability to shake walls and rattle halls. The Bass Big Muff Pi 2 features a true bypass footswitch with Latching/Momentary Action. Click the footswitch for normal latching functionality or press and hold the footswitch of a momentary burst of fuzz mayhem! The result is the Bass Big Muff Pi 2 , a new iteration of the popular design that’s been optimised for bass guitar signals. It features the same pushed-mid ‘grunt’ as the original, and promises to deliver the sustain for which the Big Muff is renowned. New to the Bass variant is a Blend knob that can be used to introduce some of the dry signal, and a Bass Boost function that delivers yet more low-end heft, even while the Tone control is set to higher values. The pedal also boasts a silent true bypass footswitch with both latching and momentary actions — clicking the footswitch offers normal latching functionality, while pressing and holding the footswitch will deliver a momentary burst of fuzz. Electro-Harmonix Electro-Harmonix Nano series browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Electro-Harmonix Bass Big Muff Pi 2 - Bass Fuzz Published on February 17, 2026 Electro-Harmonix Nano series fuzz pedal Information The Electro-Harmonix Bass Big Muff Pi 2 is an analog bass fuzz pedal that resurrects the long-lost dual op-amp gain circuit originally designed by Big Muff creator Bob Myer in the 1970s, now specifically configured and optimized for bass guitar. Developed in collaboration with Josh Scott of JHS Pedals, this modern reissue fuses the storied Big Muff legacy with a distinctive dual op-amp topology that delivers harmonically rich saturation, signature midrange grind, and virtually endless sustain while preserving foundational low-end power. Built around a unique Big Muff Pi circuit employing two dual op-amps, the Bass Big Muff Pi 2 produces thick, creamy fuzz textures ranging from classic grinding bass distortion to earthshaking doom tones. Unlike standard guitar-oriented fuzz designs, this bass-focused version integrates extended low-frequency response enhancements to ensure clarity and punch remain intact, even at high sustain settings. The pedal retains the traditional VOL, TONE, and SUSTAIN control layout associated with the Big Muff family, while adding dedicated low-end shaping tools for modern bass performance. A key addition is the BLEND control, which allows precise mixing of the dry bass signal with the distorted fuzz signal. This wet-dry mix capability enables players to maintain articulation and note definition while dialing in aggressive fuzz textures. Complementing this is a 2-position BASS BOOST toggle switch that increases overall low-end presence, particularly effective when the TONE control is set toward brighter, more treble-forward settings. Together, these features allow bassists to sculpt everything from subtle harmonic enhancement to wall-shaking fuzz without sacrificing clarity or impact. The Bass Big Muff Pi 2 features true bypass switching via a mechanical relay on a soft footswitch. In addition to standard latching operation, the footswitch supports momentary activation by pressing and holding for more than half a second, enabling temporary bursts of fuzz.
